## What's new

### Remote server: pictures, conversations after exit, panes by workspace
The phone's conversation view got several additions.

- **Pictures**: pictures from the conversation can now be shown on the phone,
  both ones attached to a prompt and ones the agent opened or captured (PNG,
  JPEG, GIF and WebP, up to 8 MB each). They appear in the chat bubbles and
  open in a full-screen viewer. This is **off by default**: switch it on with
  **Show pictures from conversations on paired devices** in **Settings >
  Remote server**. Pictures are end-to-end encrypted like everything else, but
  they cannot be redacted, so a screenshot may show secrets.
- **Prompt text with a picture**: the text of a prompt that was sent together
  with a picture was missing on the phone. It now appears.
- **After an agent exits**: when an agent ends and the pane is back at the
  shell, its last conversation stays readable on the phone. That lasts for a
  day, while ymux keeps running, or until another agent starts in that pane.
- **Panes grouped by workspace**: the phone lists panes under their
  workspace, with counts and a "needs you" badge, and each group collapses.
- **Versions**: the phone's settings list the version of the page, the server
  and each computer's yMux. Settings > Remote server shows the server's
  version. A computer whose yMux is too old for the conversation view now says
  so on the phone, instead of silently showing the screen.
- **Needs yMux-Server 0.19.0**: older combinations keep working with what both
  sides know.

### Security
- Nothing new can be done from the phone. Pictures are read-only, need the
  same view access as the conversation, and are never sent unless the new
  switch is on.
- Pictures are read only from the transcript of the agent that runs in that
  pane, never by the web page.

### Upgrade notes
- Nothing changes unless the remote server is switched on. Keep ymux and
  yMux-Server on the same minor version.
- Pictures stay off until you switch them on.
- No new keyboard shortcuts.
